original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

predecessors.relationship: Constructs and certifies the exact (3,1,1,1)->6 tensor. It screened phase A only and explicitly left phase B source/frame placement open; this package does not repeat its tensor proof.
Uses a different (2,2,1,1)->6 direct-sum tensor and strict source-event windows. This cycle screens the predecessor tensor's remaining phase-B child-order envelope.
Nearest live claim: same-column rank-one-to-rank-two retiming on gauge44. This scope changes a heterogeneous rank-three plus three rank-one profile through one rank-six child.

actual_scope: On the pinned selected provider's Phase B only, enumerate every four consecutive climb calls in child-call order with rank multiset {1,1,1,3} on four distinct registers. Defer all intervening scalar events for free, record exact source/target frames, select a maximum disjoint family, and apply the exact zero-extra-cost ceiling screen.
scope_change_reason: This is the next construction-focused placement screen explicitly left open by merged PR #1866. The child tensor is inherited rather than re-proved. To bound the smallest placement mechanism before attempting an arbitrary buffered rewrite, the search is restricted to four consecutive child calls and optimistically ignores all intervening scalar-gate costs. The rank-one-to-rank-two retiming claim #1693 has a different tensor and profile change.
bottleneck_link: Replacing one rank-three and three rank-one children by a rank-six child preserves rank mass while changing the selected local rank moment. The selected profile needs at least 135 such blocks with all extra frame, copy, scalar-routing, hosting, precision and restoration costs waived to cross the 5% ceiling target.
stop_rule: Inspect the complete pinned Phase B interval in both orientations. Enumerate four consecutive climb calls in child-call order with ranks {1,1,1,3} and distinct registers; intervening scalar events are ignored as a deliberately favorable envelope. Compute the maximum disjoint schedule and exact ceiling with zero added overhead. Stop if this upper-envelope count is below 135. Do not extend this cycle to nonconsecutive child selection, other phases, changed source words or a new block tensor.
evidence: Phase B has 3,870 events in each orientation, including 1,952 climbs. There are zero raw-event-contiguous four-climb windows of this rank shape, and exactly 12 qualifying windows after projecting away scalar events; all 12 are disjoint. Even granting every scalar move and every input/output frame, copy, hosting, precision and restoration operation for free, the exact rank-mass-preserving profile with 12 blocks has ceiling upper endpoint 0.001697288528511, only about 0.43% above the selected lower endpoint. The optimistic 5% gate first passes at 135 blocks (134 fails). No frame-compatible placement, supplier or kappa change is claimed.
